The General Officer Commanding (GOC), 1 Division, Nigerian Army, Maj.-Gen. Abubakar Wase, has urged troops to justify the Federal Government’s recent pay rise through renewed dedication, professionalism and commitment to duty. Wase, who is also the Commander, Sector 1, Operation FANSAN YAMMA, gave the charge while addressing troops of 171 Battalion in Daura, Katsina State, on Wednesday. This is contained in a statement issued by Col. Abubakar Abdullahi, Deputy Director, Army Public Relations, 1 Division Nigerian Army. Wase said the salary increase reflected the Federal Government’s appreciation of the sacrifices and selfless service of military personnel in protecting the country. He said the improved remuneration should encourage troops to strengthen their commitment to tackling security challenges and safeguarding the nation. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. The GOC reminded the troops that improved remuneration came with greater responsibilities, urging them to redouble their efforts in the discharge of their duties. “Greater remuneration comes with increased responsibilities. I urge you to redouble your efforts in tackling security challenges and safeguarding the nation,” Wase said. He charged the soldiers to remain vigilant and professional while prioritising the protection of themselves, civilians and military equipment entrusted to them. He said efforts were ongoing to ensure that troops deployed to operational areas received the necessary support to perform their assignments effectively. “Our commitment remains to ensuring that troops in operational areas receive the necessary support to carry out their assignments effectively,” he said. The GOC also addressed members of the Nigerian Army Soldiers’ Wives Association (NASWA), describing them as indispensable pillars of support for military personnel. He commended the women for their endurance and sacrifices, urging them to remain steadfast in supporting and encouraging their husbands. “Your endurance, sacrifices and support are invaluable to the morale and well-being of our troops. I encourage you to remain steadfast in supporting and encouraging your husbands,” Wase said. He added that a stable and supportive home environment contributed significantly to troops’ morale, psychological well-being and operational effectiveness. According to him, the welfare of soldiers and their families remained important to maintaining commitment and effectiveness in military operations. Abdullahi said the visit formed part of the GOC’s engagement with troops and their families to reinforce commitment to duty and promote personnel welfare.
